$comment: The one component map. typescript/scripts/ci-scope.mjs reads it to decide which CI consumers a changed path selects, and typescript/scripts/release-please-config.mjs reads the same ownership to generate release-please-config.json.
components: who owns which paths. `owns` roots minus `excludes` decide ownership, a `selectedBy` glob wins over the root, and `package` is the Cargo package.

rules: ordered, the first rule whose `paths` match a changed path decides which consumers it selects: `native` (the native Rust, tooling and E2E jobs) and `office` (the Office web checks). No match fails closed to both.
The advisory native Office browser shards are selected by consumedByNativeOffice in ci-scope.mjs, not by these rules; its verified denylist has its own tests.

Globs: `**` matches any path, `*` and `?` stay inside one directory. A rule may only narrow selection for a path that provably no job of the dropped consumer reads; ci-scope.test.ts guards each narrowed class.

rules.why: Read by build and test inputs: docs/cli-style.md by the CLI and Squad style tests, docs/NATIVE-INSTALL.md by the release archive and onboarding checks.
Prose read only by prettier in Code quality, which always runs; no test or build input reads it (guarded by ci-scope.test.ts).
The Office application and its documentation: checked by the Office web jobs only.
Rust workspace, embedded skills and the Squad extension: checked by the native jobs; the Office web checks read none of it.
Office's Rust crates are built and tested by the workspace's Cargo jobs; the Office web checks build no Rust. The advisory native Office shards are still selected by consumedByNativeOffice.
Core-only test suites and E2E scenario files: run by the native jobs. The Office image reads only the E2E harness and test support, which stay unmapped (guarded by ci-scope.test.ts).
